respuesta.razonamiento: The visual diagram and narration show a web architecture undergoing migration from legacy EC2-based services to an EKS microservices platform. Incoming traffic hits CloudFront (with static content from S3 and routing assistance from Lambda), which forwards traffic to an Elastic Load Balancer (ELB). The ELB splits traffic between frontend/legacy EC2 services, legacy systems (80%), and modern EKS microservices (20%). Both legacy systems and EKS connect to MongoDB and Kafka, while EKS also queries RDS. CloudWatch is included as a monitored service depicted on the whiteboard without direct runtime data-plane edges. Spoken monitoring mentions without visual representation (Prometheus, ELK, Slack, PagerDuty) were excluded.
respuesta.nombre: Migration from Legacy EC2 to Amazon EKS Architecture
